### 9.9 Owner questions

This section was designed on the recommendation of each, and the owner answered all of them on 2026-11-10. Each answer is given after its question, with its ledger id.

**Where the root's names live (`details-9-root-names.md`, restating `evs1-m2-24-root-directory-names`).** Lookups, listings and maps all start at the root, which today has no table. Options: (1) the root is a directory with the empty token path, its entry `idx/<repo>/<ref>/<p>.e`, moved last by the copy: a format rule, the digest's empty-path rule and EVS1-M2-46; (2) top-level names ride in sealed metadata and readers fold them: no reader can then look a top-level name up without replaying, so every no-floor top-level read would send a token or fail, and a mapper must replay from version 1; (3) a reserved first component: a visible change to every path. Recommendation: (1). **Answered: QD-612, option 1**, the root is a directory with the empty token path; EVS1-M2-46 landed it.

**How evs finds an old version's change (`details-9-index-leaf.md`).** A version written in an older epoch sits under a token evs may never be sent again. Options: (1) the fold records each folded version's place in its statement's list (two small integers per version, a marker and a table), evs proves from the place, and the reader checks the leaf against its own token: EVS1-M2-45, and four words in evs-11; (2) the entry keeps the path's token path in each epoch it lived in: up to 512 B an epoch per entry, and a second copy of old tokens in `idx/`; (3) evs scans the statement's list for the entry's hash: a 100,000-change list read whole for one file; (4) the client sends the old token when evs asks: that lets a server ask for any name's token under a removed key, which is the leak itself. Recommendation: (1). **Answered: QD-611, option 1**, the fold records each folded version's leaf place; EVS1-M2-45 landed it. QD-633 (question `evs1-m2-45-inline-leaf-place`, option 1) extends it to inline lists, which 9.2.2 and 9.2.4 now carry.

**Whether the fold deletes source copies (`details-9-fold-deletes-sources.md`).** 9.1 E and its directory form leave entries in a source that no honest map names, and the source then never drains. Options: (1) the fold deletes the source copies its push named once the current entry stands, and empties the named sources below a removed directory: a change to the landed fold, at most three DELETEs a changed path while sources stand, each one the copy then skips; (2) the copy follows a leftover through the superseded maps to learn that a newer entry replaced it: the copy must keep and chain every map and tail since the oldest source, and a removed path still has no move to follow; (3) the copy deletes whatever its map does not name: then a map that omits a live path silently loses its index entry. Recommendation: (1). **Answered: QD-607, option 1**, the fold deletes the source copies its pushes named; EVS1-M2-44 landed it.

**The push that crosses a removal (`details-9-crossing-creation.md`).** §11.6 refuses creations once a due is recorded, and the commit that records it can itself create a path under the removed key. A client that holds the removal's generation is the only party that can keep the token from being sent, and 9.2.3 has it wait. Options for evs: (1) nothing more: an old or dishonest client's crossing creation commits, and the due is recorded only by a push that commits; (2) evs refuses a creation in the crossing push, 412 PATH_EPOCH_DUE, and records the due in the refusal's fence write: a dozen lines in 5e and the refuse path, creation stops at the first push across the removal whether or not it commits, and replaying readers can hold "no creation under an epoch below an immediate removal its pin covers" as a rule. Recommendation: (2). It cannot unsend the token; it keeps §11.6's sentence true of what is committed. **Answered: QD-609, option 2**, evs refuses the crossing creation and records the due; EVS1-M2-44 landed it. QD-632 (question `evs1-m2-44-new-ref-crossing`, option 2) removes the one exemption that build kept, a ref's first push: a new ref starts in the newest epoch its creator holds, and an overlay in its base ref's current epoch (9.2.3, 9.2.6).

**A map whose source left the window (`details-9-map-source-window.md`).** A map must be bound to a head still in the 64-to-127-version window when it commits, so on a ref committing once a second a map that takes two minutes to upload never commits. Options: (1) the source may be any version at or below the head, its chain read from one log page, evs checking the tail for the versions the window holds and the mapper answering for those between its source and its base, with the copy's end LIST and replaying readers catching a miss: one cached GET at the commit; (2) keep the window and have the mapper block every push, not only creations, while it uploads: a busy ref stops for minutes at each epoch; (3) evs checks every creation since the source from log pages and push records: thousands of reads inside one commit's 5 s. Recommendation: (1). The 24 h age of a part still bounds how stale a map can be. **Answered: QD-608, option 1**, a map's source may be older than the window; EVS1-M2-44 landed it.

**Who checks a whole map (`details-9-map-verifiers.md`).** evs stores parts under a hash it never computes, and §11.9 leaves the check to readers, for whom a 1M-path map is 293 MB. Options: (1) the copy job, which reads every part anyway, checks the hash and the order and moves nothing on a mismatch, and readers check each row and entry as they use it (M1): no reader downloads a map; (2) every replaying reader downloads and checks every committed map: 293 MB a device a cut-over at 1M paths; (3) evs hashes the parts inside the PATH_EPOCH commit: 40 GETs of 7 MiB in a commit's 5 s, or the hash redefined over part hashes, a format change. Recommendation: (1). **Answered: QD-610, option 1**, the copy job checks the whole map; EVS1-M2-44 landed it.

**Questions this section builds on.** `evs1-m2-24-root-directory-names`: option 1, restated above with what a path epoch adds. `evs1-m2-16-due-classification`: option 1 as built, the client calling the same function, so a change of option changes both at once. `evs1-m2-27-every-ref-lease-epoch`: option 1; with option 3 a whole-repo subscription only loses latency on refs in other epochs. `evs1-m2-10-directory-marker-version`: option 2 as built; nothing here reads a directory marker's version but as an upper bound, and `names_leaf_*` take fields 7 and 8 so option 1's field 6 stays free. `evs1-m2-39-head-index-epoch`: option 1, **answered so (QD-640)**: format-1 code reads past a head's `index_epoch` (9.2.2); a PATH_EPOCH names no index epoch, a format-1 mapper moves `.ur-index/` entries like any others since a move writes no file, and a format-2 kind-5 segment is uploaded again by a retoken (9.2.5), which is EVS2's to carry. None of the five blocks a held task but the first, which EVS1-M2-46 built on its recommendation (QD-612). The other three stand on the option named here.

## 10. DROP lists a phone can check (§11.6, §11.7, §11.9)

Status: complete (2026-11-11)

Tasks held until complete: EVS2-M10-09, EVS2-M10-10, EVS2-M10-22, EVSB-M10-03, EVSB-M10-04.

Model: `sidecar/sidecartest/model/details/DropJob.tla`, its configurations (`DropJob.cfg`, `DropJob-*.cfg`, `DropJobWritten-*.cfg`, `DropJobTwin-*.cfg`, `DropJobProbe-*.cfg`, `DropJobReach-*.cfg`) and `run-drop.sh` beside it. New task: `.stack/plan/proposals/details-10-tasks.md` (EVS2-M10-36). Questions filed: `.stack/questions/details-10-list-commitment.md`, `details-10-drop-bounds.md`, `details-10-cite-bound.md`, `details-10-young-horizon.md`, `details-10-listed-index.md`, `details-10-head-signer.md`. Questions this section answers, each on the option 10.9 names: `plan-EVS2-drop-list-proof` (decided, QD-153, which this section keeps and bounds), `evs2-m10-03-drop-list-parts-without-changes`, `evs2-m10-04-purge-across-parts`, `evs2-m10-01-metadata-rows`. It builds to QD-626 (question `details-2-drop-job-new-ref`) and to section 8's G11 (QD-599).

### 10.1 The problem

A DROP push (§11.7) names, per lineage of a path's token paths across path epochs, the version that stays (`through_version`) and every older version by entry hash: `count` values, ascending, hashed flat into `listed_sha256`, up to 2^20 of them a path, 32 MiB. Its body, `EvsDropHistory`, is hashed flat into the statement's `drop_sha256`. §11.13's job then proves each list exact, marks what live versions still name, verifies, and deletes. Four parties decide what a DROP lists: evs's fence (5h), the job, a replaying reader, and a head reader on a phone, whose catch-up is held to 4 MiB of statements and proofs (§11.9's budget row).

Terms. For a DROP d on ref R: `u_d` is its ref version, `s_d` the instant its head write took effect, B its body. A lineage entry is a pair (e, t), a path epoch and the path's token path in it. For a version V of R: `e(V)`, `t(V)` and `k(V)` are the epoch its statement declares, the token path its change names and its path version, `u(V)` its ref version and `h(V)` its entry hash. A *candidate* is a segment or slot id a listed version names. H is evacuation's horizon (2.2.4): every batch record of a minute that starts before H has been settled.

Nine things are wrong or missing. A, C and D are the questions this problem was given, and E1 is QD-626's; B and E2 to I were found writing it.

**A. A list range cannot be checked (question plan-EVS2-drop-list-proof).** §11.9's reply row answers a listed version with "the DROP's statement, body and the list range proving membership". `listed_sha256` is SHA-256 over all the values, so a range proves nothing: a phone that reads one old version of a path whose drop lists 400,000 versions would need all 12.2 MiB of them to check one, three times its budget, and a server could send any 32 B it liked beside the hash. QD-153 took the range out and has a head reader decide from the signed body. What it did not settle is whether that is sound when the list and the body disagree, what exactly the reader compares when the entry version is withheld, and what the reply may cost (B).

**B. The body has no bound, found here.** A lineage holds one entry per path epoch the path lived through, and a ref gains an epoch at every removal of a key holder (§11.6's due row). A file at depth 8 in a team repository that has seen 300 removals has a lineage of 44.5 KiB; `ur history drop --recursive` over 1,024 such files signs a body of 44.5 MiB under one flat `drop_sha256`. A phone asked to show one of those files as dropped must fetch all of it. The lists have no total either: 1,024 paths of 2^20 values are 2^30 values, 32 GiB, more than a push's 1,024 parts can carry, and the landed seal reads every part at once.

**C. A DROP whose lists need more parts than its changes (question evs2-m10-03-drop-list-parts-without-changes).** A DROP has one change per written boundary and none per removed one. Dropping one path with 100,000 versions is one change and 3.1 MiB of list; dropping removed paths alone is no change at all. Format 1 as landed held every part to a change, so neither could be formed.

**D. Purge candidates across parts (question evs2-m10-04-purge-across-parts).** §11.13 computes a push's purge candidates per part, "a part's at part time". A rename of a versionless file removes X and creates Y from X's kind-5 segments in one push; sorted by token path, the removal falls in part 1 and the creation in part 2. Part 1's candidates subtract only part 1's versions, so they list segments Y names. The committing process's 60 s reread looks at X's newest version, now its removal, and deletes them: I-EVS-1 and I-EVS-9 broken.

**E. A first commit stalled across the job.** Three traces, one cause: the job trusts a scan of the repo's heads, and a ref with no head has none to scan.

*E1, QD-626's (`DropJobWritten-NewRef`, 17 states).* A push that creates ref N cites a listed version through `reuse`, is validated before the DROP commits, writes its record and issues its head write If-None-Match. The write stalls holding the key. With `now` the job starts 25 min later, marks and verifies over the refs that have heads, and deletes the segment. The write lands: a committed head names a deleted segment. Owner decision 204 has the job wait for the horizon to pass the DROP's commit by 2 min.

*E2, the cached head (`DropJobWritten-CachedHead`, 19 states).* Step 4 reads a reuse source's ref head from the cache (`pushAttempt.readReuse`, `HeadStore.ReadCached`), which serves an entry for 10 min. FS-91 (c) expects it: a push "validated after the commit against a cached head of the ref that a failed cache write left before the DROP" commits, and the 25 min were to cover it. So a creating push may be validated up to 10 min after the DROP's commit, and its record lies in a minute up to 10 min past it. A horizon 2 min past the commit has not settled that record. The same stalled write then lands after the deletes. Worse, the cache stamps an entry with the clock of its put (`head_cache.go`), so a process paused between a commit and its cache put serves a stale head for 10 min from whenever it wakes, and no margin covers that.

*E3, the young candidate (`DropJobWritten-YoungAdopter`, 18 states).* §11.13's young row keeps a candidate "under 25 h old at V" for a later round, so that a client that uploads its bytes again and adopts the receipt (FS-91 (e)) is found. On a ref with a head it is. A creating push that adopts the receipt at 23 h 59 min and stalls has no head at V; at 25 h 1 min the candidate is no longer young and goes; the write lands. This is section 2's finding A with the drop job in orphan GC's place.

**F. A sweep takes git history, and an adopter hides in it (section 8's G11).** A git-mode push's history segments are named by no entry version (owner decision 237). A job whose candidates were "the repo's segments no live version names" would delete every one of them at the repo's first drop (`DropJobTwin-CandidatesBySweep`, 14 states). Holding candidates to the listed versions' chains closes that, and leaves one case: a git-mode push that uploads a young candidate's exact bytes as a history segment. Its receipt is good, it commits, and no entry version names the segment, so a mark that reads entry versions alone misses it (`DropJobTwin-MarkSkipsHistory`, 20 states).

**G. Nothing finds the drop of a version once its table entry is gone, found here.** §11.9's serve row has evs answer `dropped` for each listed version and never serve an inline record of its chain. The drop table forgets an executed drop after 30 days (QD-179), "an entry absent with no void record means executed". What is left is the path entry's drop mark, which the landed fold sets only for a written boundary. A path dropped at a removed boundary has none. A marked path that is later removed loses its mark when its marker is collected, or when a path-epoch copy drains the epoch it sat in. And a record read by push id carries only the token paths of its own epoch, which evs cannot map to the path's current entry. In each case evs serves the version as if nothing had happened: its segments 404, and the reader alarms a missing segment, where FI-27 promises "never as missing or tampered"; and an inline record the drop was meant to hide, a 2 KiB file holding a leaked credential, is served again, its key in its own header.

**H. A phone that signs a drop cannot build its list, found here.** §18.5 gives a head-mode device `DropHistory`. The list is every version of the path, by entry hash. A head-mode device does not hold a path's history, and the dry run compares only a count and a hash. A phone that took the list from evs would sign what it was shown, and the list would say nothing about what its signer saw.

**I. A removed boundary's fence ends when its DROP leaves the window, found here.** 5h refuses a listed version by a bit-5 DROP in the window or by "its entry's drop mark". The fold sets a mark only where a DROP writes a version. A removed path's entry is its marker with up to four folded versions below it (§11.7's removal row), and a DROP at a removed boundary writes nothing, so that entry gets no mark. 64 to 127 commits later the DROP is paged out. A push that restores the file by citing its last version as a reuse source then finds that version in the entry, meets no DROP in the window and no mark, and commits naming segments the job deleted.

The requirement: a head reader decides whether a version is listed from at most a few hundred KiB that it can check, and never accepts as dropped a version no admin's DROP covers; a DROP of any size the format allows can be formed; no purge or drop deletes what a committed version names, however a head write stalls; no job takes what a git-mode push introduced; and a dropped version reads as dropped, and its inline content stays unserved, for the repo's life.

### 10.2 The design

#### 10.2.1 The principle

Three ideas.

**The body is the drop; the list is a check of it.** What a DROP drops is fixed by its signed body and the ref's history: every version, with an entry, of the lineage's token paths that committed on the DROP's ref below `through_version`. The list is that same set as its signer enumerated it, and it carries one more bit than the body: whether the signer's enumeration agreed with history. Only a party that holds the lineage's whole history can evaluate that bit, and each such party computes the set for itself and compares a count and a hash; none needs a byte of the list to be proved to it. So a head reader decides from the body alone (QD-153 stands), `listed_sha256` stays a flat hash, and no proof is designed. What a phone needs is a body small enough to fetch and check, so the body gets a bound.

**The resolved list is evs's index.** The job's resolve enumerates the exact listed set. It writes that set down, sorted by entry hash, and keeps it for the repo's life. An entry hash is the one name of a version that evs holds wherever it serves the version and that no path epoch, removal, collection or copy changes. evs finds the drop of a version through it, for states and for elision alike. The path entry's drop mark stays the fence's alone, and gains the one case it lacked, a removed boundary (10.2.7).

**The job waits for evacuation; it does not trust a scan of heads.** Every head write that can make a candidate reachable again is preceded by a batch record, and evacuation settles every record, fencing a pending one's ref, a ref with no head by a placeholder (2.2.3). A push can come to name a candidate in two ways only: it cites a listed version, which 5h allows only on a head that does not show the DROP; or it holds a receipt for the candidate's bytes, which 5h allows for 24 h from the object's LastModified. Each has a last minute its record can lie in. The job scans only after the horizon has passed the first, and deletes a candidate only after the horizon has passed the second. Its candidates come from the listed versions' chains and from nowhere else, and its scans count a git-mode push's new-objects list as naming what it introduced.

What does not change: `EvsPush`, `EvsDropHistory` and `EvsDropPath`, the statement's 1 KiB, `drop_sha256` and `listed_sha256` as flat hashes, sections 9 and 10, the fold's drop mark for a written boundary, marker collection, the path-epoch copy, the push route's three round trips, and the job's phases, lease and DELETE deadlines.

#### 10.2.2 Formats settled

Format 2's bytes are unfrozen until M10's exit (D-PHASE-7). Numbers are next-free in `sidecar/protocol/evs.proto` on 2026-11-11.

```proto
message EvsReadRequest {
  ...
  repeated uint64 held_drops = 11;      // DROP pushes of this ref, by ref version, whose body the reader holds and has
                                        // checked: evs sends none of them again; at most 64 (10.2.3)
}
message EvsPurgeList {
  ...
  bool replaced = 3;                    // a part's record: each replaced version's ids whole, nothing subtracted.
                                        // No purger or sweep deletes from it; the push's seal makes the candidates
                                        // from every part's (10.2.6)
}
enum EvsDropPhase {
  ...
  EVS_DROP_HORIZON = 5;                 // resolved, or between rounds: waiting for evacuation's horizon (10.2.8)
}
message EvsDropPreviewPath {
  ...
  repeated uint32 map_parts = 3;        // per older lineage entry of the request's path, the map part holding its
                                        // move, 0 the tail, as the dry run found them (10.2.4)
  bool linked = 4;                      // every older entry is a source of the one before it; false: map_parts stops
                                        // at the first that is not
}
```

`EvsPush`, `EvsPushPart`, `EvsDropHistory`, `EvsDropPath`, `EvsDropMark`, `EvsIndexEntry` and `EvsReadPathReply` keep their fields. A preview request's `EvsDropPath.map_parts` may be empty. Rules, for `protocol/EVS-FORMAT.md`:

```text
body      a DROP's body, EvsDropHistory's bytes, is at most EvsDropMaxBodyByteCount = 262,144 B; a longer one is
          INVALID, as a body off drop_sha256 is
lists     the counts of a DROP's paths sum to at most EvsDropMaxListedCount = 1,048,576 (409 DROP_LIST), so section
          10 is at most 32 MiB; a path's own count keeps its bound, which is the same number
order     section 10's values stay ascending by their bytes within a path, the paths in body order; listed_sha256
          stays SHA-256 over a path's values joined
parts     in a DROP in parts, section 9 rides whole in part 1's sections slice, and section 10's slices follow in
          part order from part 1 on; a builder cuts a slice at a value's end and puts at most
          DropListPartValueCount = 32,000 values (1,024,000 B) in a part that holds no change; a checker takes a
          slice cut anywhere, as landed
empty     a DROP with no change (removed boundaries alone, or a cancel) that passes one part states the empty
          change list of question evs1-m2-48-changeless-push-in-parts (QD-658): change_count 0, changes_root
          SHA-256 of the empty string, no changed_prefixes, every part changeless
replaced  an EvsPurgeList with replaced set rides only in a part's record; one in a push's or seal's record is
          INVALID
```

The drop table's entry (QD-179's fixed record of at most 128 B) gains one field, and the job's record its round:

```text
drop entry    drop_id 16 | ref_id 16 | push_id 16 | version u64 | place 20 | not_before_ms i64 | seen_ms i64 |
              state u8 | phase u8 | freed u64 | held u64 | preview_id 16: 126 B
              seen_ms: its appender's checked clock, read after the answer that showed it the DROP committed:
              step 7's 200 for the committing process, a cluster read of the ref's head for any other appender
job record    job_id 16 | owner 16 | until_ms i64 | phase u8 | round u32 | fence_ms i64 | horizon_ms i64 |
              cursor (file sequence u32, row u32) | retry_ms i64 | covered u16, within QD-179's 256 B
              fence_ms: the largest seen_ms of the job's covered drops; horizon_ms: the round's H
```

The job's files, `dropscan/<repo>/<job id>/<kind>-<sequence>` (QD-562's spelling), each immutable and written If-None-Match, integers big-endian:

```text
every file  "URds" | format u8 = 1 | kind u8 (1 snap, 2 cand, 3 list, 4 mark, 5 del, 6 held) | 2 zero bytes |
            repo_id 16 | job_id 16 | sequence u32 | row count u32; its rows; then SHA-256 of every byte before it
snap        sequence 0, one row per covered drop: drop_id 16 | ref_id 16 | version u64 | push_id 16 | place 20 |
            seen_ms i64. Sequence r >= 1, round r's: a first row of horizon_ms i64 and 24 zero bytes, then one
            row per ref: ref_id 16 | its head's version at M_r u64 | at V_r u64
cand        the candidates, ascending: id 32 (a slot's 16 B id zero-filled on the right) | kind u8 (1 segment,
            2 slot)
list        the listed index, whose header and tail are 10.2.9's; kept for the repo's life
mark        a first row, the scan's cursor: ref_id 16 | version u64 | 9 zero bytes; then ids as cand's rows. A
            checkpoint writes the next sequence with the ids marked since the last; the marks are their union
del         id 32 | kind u8 | outcome u8 (1 deleted, 2 absent, 3 packed, 4 young, 5 replaced, 6 held,
            7 observed): the ids answered since the last sequence; an id's newest row is its outcome
held        the ids a hold keeps, as cand's rows
```

`snap`, `cand`, `mark`, `del` and `held` go 30 d after the job ends, as today. Settings, in evs's `DropSettings` unless marked:

```text
DropStartDelay            25 min         owner decision 183's fence after not_before_ms
DropCiteBound             12 min         the job's margin past fence_ms (10.2.8); a floor no setting passes
AdoptionBound             24 h + 2 min   section 2.2.4's, the same value and floor
DropBodyReplyByteCount    1 MiB          DROP bodies in one read reply (10.2.3)
DropIndexByteCount        64 MiB         a process's listed-index and parsed-body cache, least recently used out
DropIndexRefresh          10 min         how long a process trusts its listing of a repo's list files
DropListPartValueCount    32,000         client: listed values in a part that holds no change
DropBodyKeepByteCount     4 MiB          client: checked DROP bodies kept sealed on storage, a network
HeadDropFetchByteCount    4 MiB          client: what a head-mode device fetches to build one drop's lists (10.2.4)
```

#### 10.2.3 Membership: what a reader checks, and what it costs

```text
Covers(B, e, t, k)   B a body of action 1. True iff some path p of B has (e, t) in p.lineage and k < p.through_version.
                     A removal has no entry and is covered by nothing. EvsDropLists.Lists, as landed
BodyCover(d)         the versions V of d's ref with an entry and Covers(B_d, e(V), t(V), k(V))
```

`BodyCover(d)` is the set a DROP drops. Its list is *exact* when its values are the entry hashes of `BodyCover(d)`. 10.3's L1 shows that a version in `BodyCover(d)` always committed before d did, so the set is fixed at d's commit.

**What the reply carries.** For a path whose requested version evs finds listed (10.2.9): `state` 2 or 3, `drop_id`, `not_before_ms` or `drop_version`, and the version's own statement and proof as for any version; its entry version unless it is withheld (10.2.9). Once in the reply for each drop it names: `drop_statement`, unless the reply's statements after the pin already hold it, and `drop_body`, unless the request's `held_drops` names that drop's version. evs sends at most `DropBodyReplyByteCount` of bodies in a reply; a path naming a drop past that carries the state with `drop_body` empty, and the reader reads that path again, when a body it lacks is always the reply's first. No list byte is ever sent to a reader.

**A head reader's check**, for path X read at version k, on a reply with state 2 or 3 naming drop d (`evs_drop_verify.go`):

```text
H0  k = 0, the newest version: refuse the reply as tampering. A drop never takes a path's newest version
H1  d's statement: its signature and writer, as any statement's; flags exactly 256; ref_id the ref read; its
    signer's role at its auth pin by AclState.MayDrop, with no lock there; if drop_version is above the
    reader's pin, the statement is the one its chain check placed at that version, else it is taken as
    §11.9's trusts row takes any statement below a pin
H2  the body: at most EvsDropMaxBodyByteCount, SHA-256 equal to drop_sha256, EvsCheckDropPayload's shape rules,
    action 1, not_before_ms one of its two values. A body the reader already holds for (ref, drop_version)
    is the one it checked before
H3  V's statement, as for any version: its change names tp(X, e(V)), the reader's own token for X in the epoch
    the statement declares, with base_entry_version k - 1, or 0 for a creation; where the entry version is
    served, its version is k
H4  the path p of the body with (e(V), tp(X, e(V))) in its lineage; none: the body does not cover V
H5  every entry (e, t) of p's lineage has t = tp(X, e): the lineage is this name's and no other's. An entry
    that is another name's makes the DROP invalid
H6  k < p.through_version, and V's statement's base_version is below drop_version
H7  the reader's ref history holds no cancel of d: a DROP statement of action 2 naming drop_id at
    cancels_version = drop_version, which a reader whose pin is below it has verified; one that pinned later
    takes evs's state for it, as §11.9's trusts row has it
verdict
  H1 or H2 fails        the reply is refused as any reply with a bad statement or payload hash is: an alarm,
                        nothing shown as dropped
  H5 fails              SidecarEvent history_drop, state invalid, naming the signer; nothing is dropped for this
                        reader, and a 404 of V's content alarms as a missing segment
  H3 fails              as any version whose statement does not name its path
  H4, H6 or H7 fails    evs's state is ignored: V is read as any version, and a 404 of its content alarms
  all hold              drop_pending before not_before_ms by the reader's clock, unless evs reports the drop
                        refused: readable, shown "drop pending until <time>". dropped from then on, or at any 404
                        of V's content: nothing fetched or shown, EVS_DROPPED on a read, no alarm
```

The reader computes `tp(X, e)` for each epoch of the lineage from the name and the ladder, as 9.2.1 has it read any statement in its own epoch; a lineage names only epochs at or above X's floor (10.2.4), so the check sends no token. A reader that holds no key for an epoch the lineage names cannot be a reader of the ref's current epoch (§10's ladder opens downward), so H5 is always computable. H3's `k` is the version the reader asked for, which it took from the newer version's own entry: the server chooses neither the path nor the version being judged.

**A replaying reader** makes the same checks for every path of every DROP it replays and one more, the exactness check, with no list byte fetched: it enumerates, from the history it has replayed, the versions with an entry of each lineage's token paths below `through_version`, sorts their entry hashes, and compares the count with `count` and SHA-256 over them with `listed_sha256`. A difference raises `history_drop` in state invalid and drops nothing for that reader. A replaying reader whose history starts above a lineage's oldest version (a re-pin past the budget) cannot enumerate it and judges as a head reader does, which its "verified since" mark already says.

**The reply's size.** A Signed statement is at most 1 KiB as signed, 1,168 B with its envelope; a body at most 262,144 B. So what a head reader fetches to judge every listed version under one drop is at most 263,312 B, 257.1 KiB, once, after which it holds the body: 6.3% of the 4 MiB budget, and 15 such drops fit in it. Typical is far less: one lineage at depth 8 in one epoch is 195 B, and the whole reply 1.4 KiB. Under the body's bound a `--recursive` drop of 1,024 files fits one body when a lineage averages 256 B (depth 8 or less, one epoch), and takes `ceil(1,024 x lineage / 262,099)` pushes otherwise; 10.4 has the table.

**Storage, not RAM (QD-641).** A device writes a body to its sealed store as it arrives and hashes it in a stream; it parses it path by path, holding one `EvsDropPath` at a time (at most the body's size, typically under 2 KiB), and keeps for each (repo, ref, drop version) the checked body on storage, at most `DropBodyKeepByteCount` a network, least recently used out, so later reads under the same drop name it in `held_drops` and fetch nothing.

#### 10.2.4 Building a drop

A lineage and its list are built from history the builder has verified (`evs_drop_lineage.go`, EVS2-M10-20):

```text
versions   the path's versions on the ref, newest first, from the builder's replayed history; a head-mode device
           walks them by 9.2.4's history reads (each version's statement, and its entry version for the version
           it replaces), every one checked as §11.9's reader row checks a version
lineage    one entry (e, tp(X, e)) per epoch, from the oldest epoch a walked version's statement declares up to
           the ref's current epoch for a path that stands, or the epoch its removal committed in for one that is
           removed; every epoch the ref passed through between them is included, since each link is checked
           against the map of the newer epoch (10.2.8's resolve); newest first. Every one is at or above X's
           floor (E1 of 9.2.3), so no token is sent that evs was not shown
list       h(V) for each walked version with an entry below through_version, ascending by bytes
boundary   1 when the path stands: through_version is its newest version + 1, which the DROP writes; 2 when it is
           removed: through_version is the standing removal's version
dry run    POST .../drops/preview with each path's lineage, through_version, count and listed_sha256, its
           map_parts left empty; the reply's list_match and linked must both be true, else the command stops and
           prints the resolved count; its map_parts are copied into the DROP. evs finds a link's part by binary
           search over the committed map's parts, which are runs ascending by new token path (9.2.2): a range
           read of each probed part's first move, at most 10 probes, then that part whole; the tail when no part
           holds the move
bounds     a body past EvsDropMaxBodyByteCount, or lists past EvsDropMaxListedCount, is cut into several DROP pushes
           at lineage boundaries, each previewed and confirmed as one command; one lineage that alone passes
           either bound is refused locally (ErrEvsDropTooLarge)
```

`map_parts` is the only field the builder takes from evs. Nothing rests on it but the job's own cost: it tells resolve which 8 MiB map part to read, resolve checks the move it finds there, and no reader looks at it, since a reader derives every token.

**A head-mode signer** (§18.5's `DropHistory`) builds its list by the walk above and by nothing else. It never signs a count or a hash that evs supplied. The walk fetches one statement, and one entry version where served, per version, so it is bounded by `HeadDropFetchByteCount`: about 4,000 versions at 1 KiB a statement, 8,000 at typical sizes, across all the lineages of one drop. Past it `DropHistoryPreview` answers `ErrEvsDropTooLarge`, whose message names `ur history drop` on a device that mirrors the repo. A walk that meets a version it cannot check, or a removal with no pointer behind it where the dry run then reports a larger count, stops the same way: `list_match` false. This is question `details-10-head-signer`.

#### 10.2.5 A DROP in parts

A DROP goes in parts when its one-part payload would pass 1 MiB: about 32,000 listed values beside a small body. `evs_statement.go`'s builder lays it out:

```text
1  the parts that hold changes, as for any push: the changes sorted by token path, cut into contiguous runs. A DROP
   has at most 1,024 changes, one per written boundary, each with its entry version, whose kept head rides inline
   only when it pads to at most 16 KiB (§11.7's boundary row): at most 18 parts
2  part 1's sections slice takes section 9, the body, whole: part 1's run of changes is cut to leave it room
3  section 10's values fill what room each part has left, in part order from part 1 on, a value never split;
   then parts with no change, DropListPartValueCount values each, until the lists end: at most 33 of them
4  with no change at all (step 1 empty): the statement states the empty change list (10.2.2's empty row), part 1
   holds section 9 and the first values, and every part is changeless
```

So a DROP is at most 51 parts, where a push may have 1,024. evs, per part and at the seal (`push_part.go`, `push_seal.go`):

```text
a part    steps 4 and 5 (a-e, g, h) for its entries, as for any part: a written boundary's change is an ordinary
          write of its path at part time. 5c's DROP rules that need no body: admin scope, file mode, the repo's
          kind, the format gate. Nothing of 5c's body rules, no list check, no evs_drops_per_day count. A
          changeless part runs no entry check (QD-601)
the seal  reads every part; parses section 9 from part 1 (absent there: INVALID); EvsCheckDropPayload over the
          body and section 10's slices in part order, streaming, holding one value and one hash; then, with the
          head reread from the cluster: 5c's remaining DROP rules (consent, the lock for a drop, DROP_PATH and
          VERSIONING by each written lineage's base entry, a cancel's target and time, evs_drops_per_day for a
          drop), 5h's boundary rules for each lineage against the parts' changes (a written lineage has exactly
          one change, at its newest token path, writing through_version; a removed one has none, and where its
          newest entry's epoch is current or a listed source its entry is the standing removal at
          through_version, resolve checking every removed boundary against history), DROP_LIST when the base's
          entry hash, which the part's step 4 read, is not found in that written path's values as they stream
          past, and 5h's DROPPED rerun (§11.8's seal row)
```

The one-part route makes the same checks at its step 5. `drop_sha256`, `listed_sha256` and `count` are checked where the bytes are first whole, which is the seal: a part cannot be refused for a list it holds a slice of.

#### 10.2.6 Purge candidates of a push in parts

Question evs2-m10-04's option 1, with where the ids come from made exact.

```text
a part's record   step 5 at part time, from the base versions step 4 read: for each versionless version V the
                  part replaces or removes, an EvsPurgeCandidate with V's unstaged kind-5 segment ids, its staged
                  ones and its slot ids, all of them, nothing subtracted; the list's replaced flag set. Past
                  2,048 ids or the record's 1 MiB: marked, with replaced set
the seal          reads every part. named := every id a kind-5 locator or a slot_ids entry of any part's entry
                  versions names. Its record's EvsPurgeList, replaced unset: each part's candidates in part order,
                  each less named, an emptied candidate dropped. Any part marked, or the result past 2,048 ids or
                  the record's 1 MiB: marked. Window bit 4 at step 7 when any part listed a candidate or was marked
who deletes       PurgeSink is handed the seal's list alone, on a certain commit. The sweep reads candidates from
                  push and seal records, never from a part's; a marked seal is recomputed over every part's
                  versions, as the landed recompute does (sweep_recompute.go)
rerun             a seal that reruns 5g after the head moved refuses any part whose path changed (§11.8's seal
                  row), so each part's replaced version is still its path's newest when the seal commits, and the
                  list needs no second read of any entry
```

A part's unsubtracted list is safe to store because nothing deletes from it; it is carried so the seal need not read a million entries again. `evsservice.PurgeCandidates` already subtracts every version its caller passes: the seal passes every part's.

#### 10.2.7 The fence, and the cached head

5h's DROPPED check, stated whole (`check_dropped.go`). It tests each base, each path the push deletes and each reuse source: a committed version W of ref R', read in step 4 with R''s head.

```text
window   for each entry of that head's window with bit 5 whose push is a drop (action 1), cancelled, refused or
         not: Covers(its body, e(W), t(W), k(W))  ->  409 DROPPED. Step 4 reads those bodies in its round
         (QD-389), from the process's cache or a batch range; a DROP in parts, its part 1
mark     W was read from an idx/ entry whose drop_mark has k(W) < through_version  ->  409 DROPPED
seal     a seal reruns both for every part's bases and sources against heads reread from the cluster
recorded DROPPED is recorded by the refuse row before it is answered, on a head read from the cluster
```

The mark must stand on every entry that still holds a listed version once the DROP has left the window. For a written boundary the landed fold sees to it: the DROP's written version replaces what the entry held and sets the mark, and is never skipped. For a removed boundary nothing did (10.1 I), so the fold gains one rule (`fold_format2.go`'s `dropMarksAt`, which today skips boundary 2):

```text
removed  the fold of a DROP also sets, for each lineage of boundary 2 whose newest entry (e, t) is in the head's
         current epoch or a listed source, the drop mark {drop_id, through_version} on the entry at (e, t), when
         that entry holds a marker with folded versions below it: PUT If-Match, read again on 412. A 404, or a
         marker with no version beside it, needs none: nothing is left there to cite. Like a written boundary's
         it is never skipped for a later window version, so it stands before the DROP is paged out (§11.8's step
         6 folds what it pages). An entry's mark may now equal its marker's path version, which
         ParseEvsIndexEntry refuses today
```

A listed version that is no longer in its ref's window and whose entry holds no version of it (a written boundary's replaced entry, a collected marker, a drained epoch) is not found by step 4 at all, which 5h already refuses. A cancel lifts nothing.

What bounds a citation that slips past: the head of R' that step 4 read did not show the DROP. A cluster read that did not show it was served before `s_d`. A cached head is the other way, and its staleness must be bounded by something a paused process cannot stretch:

```text
cache stamp   HeadCache stamps an entry with the head's own written_ms (§11.8's EvsHead 21: evs's clock at that
              head's write), never with the clock of the cache put, and serves it only within HeadCacheServeAge
              (10 min) of that. A put that arrives late serves for less, or not at all
```

Any head of R' that lacks the DROP was written before the DROP's own step 4 read it, so its `written_ms` is before `s_d`, and the cache stops serving it by `s_d` + 10 min. This is one line in `head_cache.go`'s `Write` (`cachedMs`, today the clock at the put), which `HeadStore.CacheCommit` calls, and it changes nothing a reader sees but how long a late put is served; `HeadStore.Commit` already stamps `written_ms` on every head write. With it:

```text
CiteLimit(d)  = s_d + 10 min + 5 s + 3 x 50 ms: every push that cites a version d lists, and whose head write can
                ever land, was validated on a head read before this, and its record lies in a minute that starts
                no later. 10 min is the cache's life; 5 s is step 7's window, inside which the record is written
                (2.2.3's record rule); 50 ms each for the clock that stamped written_ms, the one that served the
                entry and the one that named the minute
DropCiteBound = 12 min >= 10 min 5.15 s + the 50 ms by which a slow clock may put seen_ms before s_d, with the rest
                to spare
```

#### 10.2.8 The job

One job a repo (EVSB-M10-03). A job covers the pending drops whose start has passed when it is taken, with one exception that keeps a `now` drop from holding an older one back: a drop whose cite bound the horizon has not yet passed (F4) is left pending for the next job whenever some other startable drop is past its own. If every startable drop is short of its bound the job covers them and waits. A drop's states, as the table holds them:

```text
pending              -> cancelled            a cancel commits: evs's step 8 for the cancel, and the job's start read
pending              -> refused {locked}     at the start CAS, a lock standing (§8.8)
pending              -> executing/resolve    the start CAS (F1)
executing/resolve    -> refused {mismatch}   a link or a list off the ref's history; pages
executing/resolve    -> executing/horizon    cand and list files written, fence_ms in the job record
executing/horizon    -> executing/mark       the round's H read and past the cite bound (F4); H kept in the record
executing/mark       -> executing/verify     every ref scanned to its M
executing/verify     -> refused {verify}     the two scans disagree below M; pages
executing/verify     -> observed             format2.drop: observe, D recorded, nothing deleted
executing/verify     -> executing/delete
executing/delete     -> held                 a hold covers the repo: the rest of D waits (owner decision 184)
executing/delete     -> executing/horizon    D answered and some id young: the next round
executing/delete     -> done                 D answered and none young
held                 -> executing/horizon    every covering hold ended: a round over what was held
```

The fences, in the order the job meets them. Each must hold when the step that follows it is issued.

```text
F0  gate     ClockCheck.Sure(); SettlePassed() on the repo's metadata cluster and on the segment cluster;
             format2.drop on or observe; repo/ active; the job's lease more than 1 s away. Checked before every
             phase and every DELETE; any false: nothing is issued, the phase waits
F1  window   per drop, at the start CAS: not_before_ms + DropStartDelay has passed; a cluster read of its ref's
             head, and the statements from u_d to it, show no cancel of it; no lock stands. Owner decision 183
F2  exact    resolve: every lineage link found in a committed map or tail, and every list equal to BodyCover.
             The candidates are what the listed versions' chains name (G11): C
F3  seen     fence_ms := the largest seen_ms of the covered drops, each at least s_d
F4  cite     H_r, from one LIST of pb/ (OrphanHorizon, 2.2.4), is at least fence_ms + DropCiteBound. Read at the
             start of every round, before F5. Not yet: phase horizon, the lease released, retry_ms set
F5  mark     after F4's LIST: LIST head/<repo>/, then each ref's head from the cluster, then the scan to M_r
F6  verify   after F5: LIST head/<repo>/ again, each head from the cluster again, the scan to V_r, by the
             other implementation
F7  ripe     per id of D, at its DELETE: its HEAD's LastModified + AdoptionBound is at or before H_r; else young
F8  hold     per batch of DELETEs: hold/ and repo/ reread, cached at most 5 s
F9  object   each DELETE carries its lease's deadline (§11.13's clock row) and x-ur-if-unmodified-ms: its HEAD's
             LastModified (2.2.2), so a late or doubled DELETE takes the object it judged or nothing
```

F4 before F5 before F6 is the order that matters: a record the horizon has passed was settled before the LIST that gave the horizon, so a push it belongs to committed on a head the scans then read, or is dead (twin `HorizonAfterScans`).

**Start and resolve** (`drop_job.go`, `drop_resolve.go`):

```text
start(d):
  F0; clock >= d.not_before_ms + DropStartDelay
  head := cluster read of head/<repo>/<d.ref>; statements u_d+1..head.version from the window and log pages:
          a DROP of action 2 naming d  ->  cancelled (a void record), done
  a lock standing in the authorization state  ->  refused {locked} (a void record), done
  table CAS: d executing/resolve

resolve(job):                                           # reads at most 32 MB/s; killed anywhere, it runs again
  for each ref R holding a covered drop:
    scan R's log pages and window, 1..head.version: for each statement
      a PATH_EPOCH: epochs[its new epoch] := {path_map_sha256, its place, its ref version}
      else, for each change (e, t) the statement names inline; for a change list in the payload, only when
        the entry's paths_digest matches a lineage token path of that epoch and a changed_prefix covers it:
        (e, t) in some covered lineage, or a removal of a prefix of one  ->  hits += (u, e, t, entry_sha256,
        base_entry_version)
    for each hit with an entry: read its entry version from its push's record; k := its version
    for each covered drop d on R, each path p:
      links   for i in 1..len(p.lineage)-1, newer := p.lineage[i-1], older := p.lineage[i], m := p.map_parts[i-1]:
                m = 0: the tail of epochs[newer.e]'s push (its payload's tail moves)
                m > 0: part m of pmap/<repo>/<R>/<newer.e>/<epochs[newer.e].path_map_sha256>/, its Signed bytes
                       checked against that hash's part order as the copy checks them
                holds a move with new_token_path = newer.t and a source (older.e, older.t), else {mismatch}
      set     S := the hits with an entry, (e, t) in p.lineage, u < u_d and k < p.through_version
      exact   |S| = p.count and SHA-256 over S's entry hashes ascending = p.listed_sha256, else {mismatch}
      bound   boundary 1: d's own statement writes p.lineage[0] at base p.through_version - 1, and every hit of
              the lineage below u_d has k < p.through_version; boundary 2: the newest hit of the lineage below
              u_d is a removal, of the path or of a directory holding it, whose version is p.through_version;
              else {mismatch}
      a mismatch: the job reads section 10's values for p and logs how many of S they lack and how many they
              add, with the first of each, for the page; d refused {mismatch} (a void record)
    C += every segment id a kind-1 locator of a version in S names and every slot id it names, less ids
         that versions in S name only through kind-5 locators (§11.13's resolve row)
    list file rows += (entry_sha256, d, inline) for each V in S, inline when its chain holds a kind-2 locator
  write list-*, then cand-*, then snap-0 with fence_ms; table CAS: executing/horizon
```

A drop refused at resolve leaves the job's other drops as they are: each covered drop is resolved and refused alone, and C is the union over those not refused.

**A round** (`drop_job.go`, `drop_mark.go`, `dropverify/verify.go`, `drop_delete.go`):

```text
round(job, r):
  F0
  H_r := OrphanHorizon(metadata cluster)                       # one LIST(pb/, limit 1): F4
  H_r < fence_ms + DropCiteBound  ->  phase horizon; retry_ms := max(now + 10 min,
                                       fence_ms + DropCiteBound + 25 h); release the job; return
  job record: round r, horizon_ms H_r                           # by CAS, before any scan

  refs := LIST head/<repo>/                                     # after the horizon: F5
  for each ref: head := cluster read (a held key: 503, the phase waits and retries; never skipped)
                M_r[ref] := head.version; mode := head.ref_mode
                scan pushes (M_{r-1}[ref], M_r[ref]], a new ref from 1: marks += the ids of Names(push) in C
  checkpoint marks and the cursor at most once a minute

  refsV := LIST head/<repo>/                                    # F6, by dropverify
  for each ref: head := cluster read; V_r[ref] := head.version
                scan pushes 1..V_r[ref] in round 1, (V_{r-1}[ref], V_r[ref]] after: for each id of
                Names(push) in C and not in marks:
                  the push at or below M_r[ref]  ->  refused {verify}: the scans disagree; pages; nothing
                                                     more is deleted
                  the push above M_r[ref]        ->  marks += id; count urnetwork_evs_drop_late_marks_total
  reread each covered drop's ref for a cancel and the repo for a lock (§11.13's verify row)
  observe mode: write del-* with D := C - marks, every outcome observed; state observed; return

  D := C - marks - ids already answered
  for each id of D, at most 10 a second, by the cursor:
    F0, F8
    HEAD the object (seg/ on the segment cluster, slot/ on the metadata cluster)
      404 with a spidx/ entry: packed; any other 404: absent
      LastModified + AdoptionBound > H_r: young                                   # F7
      else DELETE with the lease's deadline and WithBlobUnmodified(LastModified)  # F9
        204: deleted, its stored size reported once (§11.13's delete row)
        412: replaced: the id was stored again since the HEAD; it is not this drop's
        held key or unknown outcome: unanswered; the cursor does not pass it
  young left: phase horizon, retry_ms := the least young bound + 25 h; the next round's F4 reads H again
  none left: done
```

`Names` is what a scan counts a committed push as naming, and both implementations hold to it:

```text
Names(P)   for each entry version E of push P that is live: every segment id of a kind-1 or kind-5 locator of
           E, and every slot id E names; and, when the ref is git mode, every segment id of P's new-objects list
           (its history segments are named by nothing else: G11)
live       E is live unless a list file holds h(E) under a drop this job covers and did not refuse, or under one
           the table shows done or held, or no longer shows and holds no void record for: §11.13's "no executing
           or done drop lists", by entry hash. A pending, cancelled, refused or observed drop's versions are live
```

A later round's scans read only versions after the earlier round's, since history below a snapshot does not change and marks only grow; its `LIST head/` finds a ref created since. A held drop's resume is a round whose D is the held ids.

**What the waits cost a drop.** A drop with the 7-day window meets F4 already passed: its `seen_ms` is a week old. A `now` drop waits until the horizon passes `seen_ms` + 12 min, which evacuation's hourly run brings 25 h 12 min to 26 h 12 min after its commit; owner decision 204's "about 25 to 26 h" stands, 10 min later. F7 adds nothing for a candidate over 49 h old, which is every candidate of a 7-day drop. A `now` drop of a version uploaded an hour before it deletes that version's segments about 48 h after the drop, where §11.13 as written says 25 h; question `details-10-young-horizon` puts that to the owner.

#### 10.2.9 Serving: the drop of a version, and the listed index

**The listed index.** Resolve writes the exact listed set of the job's drops, for the repo's life:

```text
dropscan/<repo>/<job id>/list-<sequence>     on the segment cluster, If-None-Match, at most 131,072 rows a file
  header   10.2.2's, kind 3, then drop count u16 | 2 zero bytes | per drop: drop_id 16 | ref_id 16 | version u64 |
           push_id 16
  rows     entry_sha256 32 | drop u16, an index into the header's drops | flags u8 (1: its chain holds an inline
           record): 35 B, ascending by entry_sha256 then drop within a file
  index    the entry_sha256 of every 128th row, from the first, 32 B each
  bloom    10 bits a row, rounded up to a byte; 7 probes at (a + i x b) mod bits, a and b the first and second
           8 B of the entry_sha256, big-endian, i = 0..6
  tail     index offset u32 | bloom offset u32, then the file's SHA-256 (10.2.2): together its last 40 B
```

A drop refused after resolve keeps its rows; a void record outranks them. The files leave only with the repo's shred.

**The lookup** (`read_drop.go`). evs holds, for a version V it is about to serve, `e(V)`, `t(V)` and `h(V)` from V's own statement and `k(V)` from its entry version or, withheld, from the request.

```text
DropOf(V):
  0  drops/<repo>/_ absent (a GET cached 5 s, as repo/ is): none. A repo that never had a drop pays this alone
  1  live drops, newest first: each table entry on V's ref in state pending, executing, held, done or observed
     with version > u(V), and each bit-5 entry of the ref's window the table lacks (its DropSink append is
     made again): Covers(body, e(V), t(V), k(V))  ->  that drop
  2  each list file of the repo: bloom, then index, then one range read of 128 rows (4,480 B): a row with h(V)
     whose drop has no void record  ->  that drop
  3  none
state(V, d):  d pending and evs's clock before d.not_before_ms: drop_pending; else dropped
```

Step 1 answers from a drop's commit, before any job has run, and for every drop still in the table. Step 2 answers for the repo's life. Both give the same answer for a drop that resolved, since its list is exact. A process learns a repo's list files by one LIST of `dropscan/<repo>/` each `DropIndexRefresh`, reads each file's header, then its last 40 B, then its index and bloom by one range read from the index offset, and keeps them, with parsed bodies, within `DropIndexByteCount`. The whole file's hash is checked by whoever reads it whole: resolve when it writes, and the rebuild of 10.5.

**What is withheld** (§11.9's serve row), from `not_before_ms`, for a version whose `DropOf` is a drop not cancelled or refused:

```text
content    nothing of a kind-1 segment or slot the job's del or held files name (the withheld-id set of
           EVS2-M10-10, loaded through the table, as planned): 404
entry      the entry version of a version whose chain holds a kind-2 locator is not served: the path reply
           carries the statement and the state with version.entry_version empty
records    in any range of a push's or part's record that evs serves, by path, by history or by push id, the
           bytes of each such entry version are sent as zeros of the same length. Offsets, lengths and frames
           stay valid, every other entry version keeps its hash, and a reader that finds an entry version all
           zero under a path it holds as dropped raises no alarm (EVS2-M10-22's replay over an elided part)
```

evs applies `records` to each entry version of the record it serves that holds a kind-2 locator, by `DropOf`; a record with no inline record costs nothing. evs's `refused` report stays unsigned and only lets a reader show content still stored.

### 10.3 Invariants and why they hold

```text
readers (10.2.3)
L1  BodyFixed      for a committed DROP d whose links hold, BodyCover(d) is the versions with an entry of the
                   lineage's token paths that committed on d's ref before u_d; nothing that commits later joins it
L2  ListIsBody     d's list is exact iff its values are the entry hashes of BodyCover(d); so for a drop that
                   executes, a version is listed iff the body covers it
L3  HeadSound      a head reader shows a version as drop_pending or dropped only if a DROP on that ref, signed by
                   a device holding the drop right at its pin, covers that version of that name by a lineage that
                   is wholly that name's; never a path's newest version
L4  ReplyBound     a reader fetches at most 263,312 B to judge every version one drop lists, and no list byte
the fence (10.2.7)
C1  CiteLimit      a push that cites a version d lists and whose head write can land was validated before
                   s_d + 10 min 5.15 s, and its record lies in a minute that starts no later
the job (DropJob.tla)
ClosureHolds       I-EVS-1 and I-EVS-15: every committed version that no executed drop lists keeps every id it
                   names, a git-mode push's history segments included, however late its head write landed
OnlyCandidates     FI-27 (2) and G11: the job deletes nothing but ids a listed version's chain names
DeletesGated       no DELETE before a round took the horizon
HeadsRise          a placeholder head exists only with its fence raised (2.3's, kept)
JobEnds            every job that starts ends, done, once its waits have room (liveness)
serving and parts
S1  Found          DropOf finds the drop of every version an executed drop lists, for the repo's life, whatever
                   became of its path's entry
S2  Unserved       from not_before_ms no inline record of a version a drop lists is served, by any route, unless
                   the drop is cancelled or refused
P1  Formable       every DROP within 10.2.2's bounds can be laid out, in at most 51 parts
P2  PurgeWhole     a push in parts lists as a purge candidate no id a version of that push names
```

**Why L1 and L2.** Take a path p of d with boundary 1. At d's commit 5g held (I-EVS-8): the version d writes at p's newest token path, `through_version` T, is that path's newest committed version plus one. So every version of that token path that committed before `u_d` is below T. A version of it that commits after `u_d` is above T: it replaces T or a later version, or it is a creation after a removal, whose version is `max(b, m) + 1` with m the removal's version, itself above T, or, the marker collected, with b at or past the removal's ref version (§11.7's collect row: `folded_through >= r + 64`), which no path version exceeds. An older lineage entry (e', t') names the same path in an earlier epoch, which is what resolve's link check establishes; no push commits in an epoch after the cut-over that left it (412 PATH_EPOCH), so each of its versions committed before `u_d`, and each is below T because a path's versions never restart. With boundary 2, T is the standing removal's version: every version of the lineage before the removal is below T, none committed between the removal and `u_d` (it stands), and a re-creation is above T as before. So `Covers` picks out exactly the versions with an entry that committed on the lineage's token paths before `u_d`, and that set cannot grow. L2 is then the definition of resolve's `exact` row: resolve computes the same set from the ref's statements and compares a count and a SHA-256 over 32 B values, which collide for no two different sets anyone can find.

**Why L3.** H1 gives a statement a holder of the drop right signed, for this ref. H2 binds the body to it. H4 and H6 give `Covers(B, e(V), tp(X, e(V)), k)` with the name X and the version k the reader chose and the token its own key derived, and H3 ties the statement being shown to that same token and version; H5 makes p's lineage X's in every epoch it names, so p is "the drop of X". By L1 that is membership in `BodyCover(d)`. Nothing in the check is the server's word but the unsigned report that a drop was refused, which can only let content be shown. What a server gains against a head reader is what §11.9's dropped row already states: it can withhold what an admin's body covers. It cannot have a version outside every admin's body accepted as dropped, so it cannot delete live history under a phone's eyes: such a version's 404 alarms. The head reader and the replaying reader differ in one case only, a DROP whose signer's own list disagrees with its own body: the replaying reader calls it invalid, the head reader takes the body. That DROP never executes (F2), and evs reports it refused.

**Why L4.** A Signed statement is at most 1 KiB as signed (§11.6's size row); with the Signed envelope's ids and signature, 1,168 B. The body is at most 262,144 B: evs refuses a longer one before it commits, and a reader stops reading a `drop_body` at that length before it hashes it, so the bound holds against a server that lies. 1,168 + 262,144 = 263,312 B. 10.4's table gives a lineage's size for each depth and epoch count, computed from the wire sizes for a `through_version` under 2^35 and map parts under 2^14: a token is 18 B with its tag and length, a lineage entry's own tag, length and epoch 4 to 7 B, a map part 2 B, and `through_version`, `boundary`, `count` and `listed_sha256` together at most 46 B. The Merkle root that question `details-10-list-commitment`'s option 2 would add has the bounds 10.9 quotes: an inclusion path in an RFC 9162 tree of n leaves is at most `ceil(log2 n)` hashes, since the tree splits at the largest power of two below n and the left subtree is never the shallower, which is 20 hashes, 640 B, at 2^20; a script checked that for every n to 2^20, and for every leaf of every tree to 4,096 leaves, and found every contiguous range of every tree to 256 leaves provable with at most `2 ceil(log2 n)` hashes beside its leaves.

**Why C1.** A citation passes 5h only against a head of the cited version's ref that does not show d (10.2.7's window and mark rows; a head that shows d has d in its window, or d folded: a written boundary's entry replaced and marked, a removed boundary's marker entry marked, or the listed version nowhere step 4 looks). A head from the cluster that does not show d was read before `s_d`. A head from the cache was written before d's own step 4 read it, so its `written_ms` is under `s_d` + 50 ms, and the cache serves it for under 10 min more by a clock within 50 ms. Step 7 is issued within 5 s of step 4's reads and the record is written in between (2.2.3's record rule), in a minute that began no later than 50 ms past its append (the minute rule). A process paused after its last check sends its write late, but its record was written before the pause. So the record's minute starts before `s_d` + 10 min + 5 s + 150 ms.

**Why the job is safe (ClosureHolds).** Let the job delete x in round r. Then x is in C; no scan of round r or before found a live version naming x; `H_r` came from a LIST at `t_H` issued before round r's LISTs of `head/` and reads of heads; `H_r >= fence_ms + DropCiteBound`; and `LastModified(x) + AdoptionBound <= H_r` for the object the DELETE names (F9). Suppose a committed version W, listed by no executed drop, names x after the DELETE. W's push P passed 5h for x in one of two ways.

1. *P introduced x on a receipt.* The receipt is for this object, so P's last check passed within 24 h of an `upload_ms` at most 100 ms past its LastModified, and by 2.3's arithmetic P's record lies in a minute that starts before `LastModified + AdoptionBound`, which is at or before `H_r`. Every record of a minute before `H_r` was settled before `t_H` (2.2.4). Settled means committed on a head, visibly, or dead for good, its ref fenced, a ref with no head by a placeholder that the stalled write lost to (2.3's step 5). If it committed, it did so before `t_H`, its ref had a head when round r listed `head/`, and the scan to `M_r` read its version and counted x in `Names`, an entry version's locator or, for a git-mode push's history segment, the new-objects list: x was marked. If it is dead, W does not exist.
2. *P cites a committed version W' that names x* (its base, a path it deletes, or a reuse source). Take the first such W in commit order. W' committed before W, so the scans read W', or W' is itself a live version naming x that they missed, which the choice of W rules out. Had W' been live when they read it, it would have marked x. So W' is listed by a drop d that this job covers or that an earlier job executed. Then by C1 P's record lies in a minute before `s_d` + 10 min 5.15 s, which is before `seen_ms(d) + DropCiteBound`, at or before `fence_ms + DropCiteBound` and so before `H_r` (an earlier job's d has an older `seen_ms` still). The record was settled before `t_H`, and as in 1 the scans saw W or it does not exist.

Both ways contradict x being unmarked. A version an executed drop lists may lose what it names: that is the drop. A later upload of the same bytes is a new object, which the DELETE's LastModified refuses.

**Why OnlyCandidates.** C is built in resolve from the locators and slot ids of versions in S and from nothing else, and D is a subset of C. The job never lists `seg/`. A history segment is in C only if a listed version's chain also names its id, which needs equal bytes; then the git-mode push that introduced it is counted by `Names` and marks it.

**Why JobEnds.** Evacuation settles every record once its minute is 25 h old, a held key first released by §19.6's settle rule, a ref with no head fenced by a placeholder (2.3's RecordsLeave). So the horizon passes any fixed time, F4 opens, and each young id's bound is passed in turn; a round that finds an id ripe deletes or marks it, and C is finite.

**Why S1 and S2.** A drop that executes resolved, and resolve wrote a row for the entry hash of every version in `BodyCover(d)` before the job's first DELETE (the list files precede the cand file and the phase change). The files are immutable and stay until the repo's shred. evs holds a version's entry hash wherever it serves the version: in its statement's change, inline or by proof. So step 2 of `DropOf` needs no path entry, token of a current epoch, marker or mark. Before resolve, and for 30 d after, step 1 gives the same answer from the body by L2. S2 follows: every route that serves an entry version passes through `DropOf` for those whose chain holds an inline record.

**Why P1 and P2.** 10.2.5's layout: 1,024 changes with inline kept heads of at most 16 KiB each are at most 17 MiB, 18 parts; a body of at most 256 KiB fits part 1 beside a shortened run; 2^20 values at 32,000 a part are 33 parts: 51 in all, and question evs1-m2-48's empty change list covers the DROP with no change. For P2, the seal subtracts from each replaced version's ids every id any part's entry versions name, and it reads every part; no deleter reads a part's list.

**The model.** `DropJob.tla` starts where `EvsCommit.tla`'s drop stories end: a DROP whose list is exact commits on ref A, listing the one version that names segment s1. Three other refs take the pushes that may still come to name s1: B, file mode with a head; N, with no head, whose first commit creates it If-None-Match; and G, git mode, whose one committed push introduced the history segment sh. A push names s1 by citing the listed version (passing 5h until the DROP commits, and for `CacheLife` ticks after on a cached head), by a receipt for its bytes (passing for `ReceiptLife` ticks), or, on G, by a receipt for its bytes as a history segment. Each attempt reads its head, checks, writes its batch record, and issues a head write that lands, fails, stalls holding its key or is sent late by a paused process, as in `EvsGc.tla`. The evacuator settles each record 3 ticks old, fencing a pending one's ref, N by a placeholder. The job starts, resolves, takes the horizon, marks, verifies and deletes, with young rounds; its start, which reads the DROP committed, stands for the appender whose clock gives `seen_ms`. Time is ticks: a receipt lasts 3, a cached head hides the DROP for 2, and the job's margin is 2. The model's ASSUME holds the two sums of 10.2.7 and 2.3 in the design's milliseconds.

Runs, TLC at the owner's jar (master d8fb231), each breadth-first over every reachable state at its bounds. `run-drop.sh` stops a run whose state directory passes 8 GB and deletes each run's state directory as it ends.
